records.name: Antibody-drug conjugate (ADC)
records.tldr: An antibody-drug conjugate links a target-binding antibody to an active drug. Binding, delivery, release and drug action each matter, and normal tissues can also be exposed.
records.summary: The antibody recognizes an accessible antigen; the attachment chemistry and linker affect stability and release; the payload acts through its own molecular mechanism. Cytotoxic examples include TOP1 inhibitors, tubulin inhibitors and DNA-damaging agents. Uptake and lysosomal processing are important for many constructs, while some linkers also release drug outside cells. A surface antigen can be a delivery address without being a driver the tumor depends on. The dose, mean loading, loading distribution, released species and exposure must be interpreted for the finished product. There is no universal fold improvement in the therapeutic window.

notes: The treatment and diagnostic labels retain product-specific indications and testing requirements. A companion diagnostic validated for one drug or intended use is not automatically interchangeable with another. Keep the study population, comparator and prior exposure with any clinical result; a binding result or shared antigen name does not transfer benefit.

Lymphoma: binding and antigen abundance do not by themselves establish usable payload delivery. Internalization, intracellular processing and payload transport need construct-specific evidence. CD20 is not universally non-internalizing: rituximab-CD20 uptake varied with target-cell Fc-gamma receptor IIb in the cited experiments. Lysosomal-transporter experiments with other conjugates also show that a block after uptake can cause resistance. These observations do not establish one limiting toxicity for all lymphoma ADCs.
records.principle: Binding can support delivery, but uptake, processing, access to the payload’s target and cellular response require separate evidence.
records.generation: Attachment chemistry, payload and delivery format vary across products
strengths: Can deliver an active drug through a selected molecular address
Some constructs kill neighboring target-negative cells in defined models
limitations: Normal-tissue exposure and product-specific lung, blood-cell, nerve or eye toxicity remain possible
Antigen, trafficking, release, efflux and cell-response changes can cause resistance
Binding or an expression score alone does not establish benefit

records.name: Site-specific conjugation & linker chemistry
records.tldr: Attachment sites, loading and linker chemistry shape the finished conjugate. More controlled manufacture can help, but safety and effectiveness require evidence for that product.
records.summary: Conventional attachment to available lysines or reduced cysteines can produce mixtures of attachment sites and loading states. Engineered sites and other selective chemistries aim to control these features. In one engineered-cysteine study, a near-homogeneous anti-MUC16 conjugate retained mouse antitumor activity and was tolerated at higher doses in rats and monkeys than its conventional comparator. That result supports a design strategy, not a guarantee of identical loading or improved human outcomes for every site-specific product. Hydrophilic drug-linker designs have also reduced accelerated clearance in studied high-loading constructs.

links.label: Junutula et al.: engineered-cysteine conjugation and animal therapeutic index (2008)
Lyon et al.: hydrophobicity, loading and conjugate pharmacokinetics (2015)
Hamblett et al.: drug loading in one anti-CD30 conjugate, cell and mouse experiments (2004)
Goldenberg et al.: sacituzumab govitecan and gradual SN-38 release (2015)
Tomabechi et al.: lysosomal transport of a T-DM1 catabolite (2022)

notes: Protease cleavage, hydrolysis or reduction can release a payload from appropriate cleavable linkers. Noncleavable designs rely on antibody breakdown and can leave an active linker-bearing catabolite. HIC, mass spectrometry, attachment-site mapping and stability assays answer different characterization questions; an average DAR or the name of a platform does not establish equivalence.
records.principle: Attachment site, site occupancy, linker chemistry and released chemical species are separate properties of the complete conjugate.
strengths: More control of attachment and loading in suitable designs
Can support defined single- or multiple-payload constructs
limitations: Loading distribution and impurities still require measurement
Stability, aggregation, exposure and safety remain product-specific

records.name: Linker (ADC)
records.tldr: The linker connects antibody and payload. Its chemistry affects where the drug separates and which active chemical species becomes available.
records.summary: Cleavable linkers can respond to enzymes, reduction or hydrolysis under specified conditions. Release is construct-specific and need not occur exclusively inside a cancer cell. A noncleavable linker can remain on the payload while the antibody is broken down, leaving an active amino-acid-linker-payload catabolite. For T-DM1, Lys-SMCC-DM1 must leave the lysosome to reach its intracellular site of action; SLC46A3 directly transports this catabolite in experimental systems. The released species can differ from the unconjugated parent drug in transport and permeability.

links.label: Goldenberg et al.: sacituzumab govitecan and gradual SN-38 release (2015)
Tomabechi et al.: lysosomal transport of a T-DM1 catabolite (2022)
Ogitani et al.: released-species permeability and local bystander killing in models (2016)
Lyon et al.: hydrophobicity, loading and conjugate pharmacokinetics (2015)

notes: The T-DM1 catabolite has low membrane permeability in the cited comparison; that is not a chemical rule that every noncleavable catabolite is impermeable. Bystander activity depends on release, diffusion, local concentration and neighboring-cell susceptibility. Linker hydrophilicity can mitigate hydrophobicity in particular designs without guaranteeing freedom from aggregation or toxicity.

records.name: Drug-to-antibody ratio (DAR)
records.tldr: DAR usually reports the average number of payload molecules attached per antibody. The average can hide a mixture of differently loaded molecules.
records.summary: Drug-to-antibody ratio describes payload loading. A preparation can contain antibodies with different numbers and sites of attachment, so the reported mean does not specify every molecule. Two preparations with the same mean can differ in their loading distribution and attachment chemistry. Higher loading can increase cell-assay potency while also changing hydrophobicity, aggregation, clearance and tolerated exposure. Hamblett and colleagues separated differently loaded versions of one anti-CD30 conjugate and found that greater cell-assay potency did not translate into a proportional mouse treatment advantage. That experiment does not set one optimal DAR for every product.

links.label: Hamblett et al.: drug loading in one anti-CD30 conjugate, cell and mouse experiments (2004)
Junutula et al.: engineered-cysteine conjugation and animal therapeutic index (2008)
Lyon et al.: hydrophobicity, loading and conjugate pharmacokinetics (2015)

notes: Site-directed attachment can improve control, but occupancy, remaining heterogeneity, stability and function still need measurement. Hydrophobic-interaction chromatography and suitable mass-spectrometric methods can characterize loading; an average alone cannot establish product equivalence or clinical benefit. For multiple payload types, retain each component’s loading instead of inventing its share from total DAR.

records.name: Bystander effect (ADC)
records.tldr: A conjugate can harm neighboring cells when an active released species reaches them, including neighbors with little or none of the delivery target.
records.summary: Bystander killing is a local drug effect, distinct from radiation crossfire or immune memory. It depends on the chemical species actually released, its transport through membranes and tissue, the concentration reaching neighboring cells and their susceptibility. Ogitani and colleagues compared a permeable DXd species, a poorly permeable alternative and the T-DM1 catabolite Lys-SMCC-DM1. Their coculture and mixed-tumor mouse experiments showed neighboring target-negative-cell killing with the permeable DXd construct; a separate target-negative tumor on the opposite flank did not respond in that experiment. These findings support a local mechanism in those models, not a universal safety or patient-benefit claim.

links.label: Ogitani et al.: released-species permeability and local bystander killing in models (2016)
Goldenberg et al.: sacituzumab govitecan and gradual SN-38 release (2015)

notes: Neither a cleavable-linker label nor a permeability result alone proves bystander killing in a tumor. More chemical spread can also expose normal cells, so it is not an efficacy ranking.

records.name: Cross-resistance
records.tldr: Resistance to one treatment can also reduce sensitivity to another when the treatments share a vulnerable step. A different drug name does not establish an independent mechanism.
records.summary: For antibody-drug conjugates, resistance can involve antigen access or uptake, intracellular processing and transport, the payload’s molecular target, drug efflux, or the cell’s response to injury. Breast cancer models selected for resistance to T-DXd or sacituzumab govitecan showed shared payload-associated resistance and renewed activity with some non-TOP1 conjugates. A selected patient cohort and functional experiments also linked particular TOP1 mutations to reduced sensitivity to SN-38 and deruxtecan. These are distinct forms of evidence, not proof that every resistant tumor has the same cause or that switching class improves outcomes for everyone.

links.label: Rampa et al.: acquired ADC resistance and payload switching in breast cancer models (2026)
Abelman et al.: selected patient samples and functional TOP1-mutant experiments (2025)
Kinneer et al.: lysosomal-transporter loss and resistance to noncleavable conjugates (2018)

notes: Changing the antibody target can leave shared efflux or cell-response resistance intact. Changing payload mechanism can leave a delivery or processing defect intact. A transporter may handle more than one drug, and different tumor cells can carry different resistance mechanisms. Collateral sensitivity is the separate possibility that adaptation to one treatment increases sensitivity to another.

records.name: ADC sequencing
records.tldr: ADC sequencing asks whether a second conjugate can help after the first fails, especially when it carries the same payload class. The earlier response and reason for stopping matter.
records.summary: A second conjugate may retain activity after a first, but neither shared nor different target names settle the outcome. Payload cross-resistance, altered delivery and tumor evolution can all matter. Retrospective treatment sequences are affected by who lived long enough and remained fit to receive another drug, treatment line, prior response and clinician selection. A selected cohort with post-treatment plasma profiling and laboratory TOP1-mutant experiments supports a resistance hypothesis; cell and mouse payload-switching experiments test a different question. Neither design establishes the best clinical sequence.

links.label: Abelman et al.: selected patient samples and functional TOP1-mutant experiments (2025)
Rampa et al.: acquired ADC resistance and payload switching in breast cancer models (2026)
Kinneer et al.: lysosomal-transporter loss and resistance to noncleavable conjugates (2018)

notes: Mechanism experiments can compare an intact conjugate with its free payload, measure uptake and released species, and perturb a suspected transporter or resistance gene. These experiments require controls and do not by themselves validate a clinical test for choosing the next ADC. A trial in ADC-naive patients cannot establish effectiveness specifically after progression on a prior TOP1 ADC.

records.name: Bispecific ADC
records.tldr: A bispecific antibody-drug conjugate uses two recognition features to deliver a payload. Its design can change delivery; phase 3 testing still evaluates the complete drug.
records.summary: Different-antigen designs recognize two proteins; biparatopic designs recognize distinct epitopes on one protein. Depending on the molecule and cell, the design may favor binding to either target, combined binding, receptor clustering or transport through an internalizing partner. A biparatopic HER2 conjugate carrying a tubulysin derivative promoted clustering and lysosomal trafficking in preclinical models. A separate HER2-by-prolactin-receptor study increased uptake and cell killing by linking a slower-trafficking target to a rapidly internalized partner. These experiments do not isolate a universal clinical advantage of two-target binding. Clinical examples need their own evidence: the registry identifies izalontamab brengitecan (EGFR-by-HER3) in the phase 3 BL-B01D1-307/PANKU-Breast02 study of previously treated advanced triple-negative breast cancer against chemotherapy. That design does not isolate the added contribution of the bispecific format over another ADC.

links.label: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06382142: BL-B01D1-307
ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06304974: PANKU-Esophagus01 (BL-B01D1-305)
BCG033 PTK7-by-TROP2 conjugates: preclinical AACR abstract (2024)
Li et al.: biparatopic HER2 conjugate in preclinical models (2016)
Andreev et al.: HER2 and prolactin-receptor trafficking experiments (2017)

notes: A bispecific ADC is distinct from a T-cell engager and from a dual-payload ADC. Measure each recognition interaction, tissue expression, uptake, processing and function; a single target score is not a universal eligibility rule. The clinical-program records retain study-specific evidence. A trial against chemotherapy does not by itself measure the added contribution of the bispecific format over a matched conventional ADC.
records.principle: Recognition geometry, avidity, target distribution and intracellular trafficking must be tested for the complete construct.
strengths: Can alter recognition or intracellular delivery in suitable designs
Offers a way to test heterogeneous target expression
limitations: Healthy cells may express one or both targets
Two binding specificities do not establish two payload mechanisms
Selectivity, loading, release and toxicity require construct-specific evidence

records.name: Monoclonal antibodies
records.tldr: A monoclonal antibody is a manufactured protein with a defined recognition design. Its other functional parts and the target biology determine what follows binding.
records.summary: Monoclonal does not by itself mean patient-specific or physically identical molecules in every detail. A therapeutic preparation can contain characterized molecular variants, including different sugar modifications. Recognition can be used to block an interaction, recruit immune effectors, carry a drug or radionuclide, or bridge cells, depending on the complete product. A shared target name does not establish the same epitope or action. Binding, functional activity, exposure and clinical benefit answer different questions.

links.label: NCI: monoclonal antibodies and distinct immune actions
FDA Q6B: characterization, molecular heterogeneity and biological activity
Li et al.: one recognition format can alter trafficking and activity in models (2016)
Lim et al.: rituximab-CD20 internalization in B-cell malignancies (2011)
Kinneer et al.: lysosomal-transporter-dependent conjugate resistance (2018)

notes: FDA Q6B separates protein quantity, biological activity and quality characterization. Identity, purity, aggregation, heterogeneity and stability tests address different attributes. A potency result needs a defined assay and reference; protein mass alone does not measure the same quantity. These manufacturing measurements do not replace clinical evidence.

Lymphoma: internalization is not an immutable property of the antigen name. Lim and colleagues found that target-cell Fc-gamma receptor IIb promoted internalization of rituximab-CD20 complexes, with substantial variation across the studied B-cell malignancies. This changes antibody exposure and access for effector cells; it does not establish that any particular CD20 conjugate will deliver an effective or safe payload.
records.principle: A defined recognition region makes contact; the assembled product and biological setting determine the tested effect.
strengths: Defined molecular recognition can support different therapeutic mechanisms
limitations: Healthy tissue can share the recognized target
Human or humanized sequence does not establish freedom from adverse effects
Identity or binding alone does not establish potency or clinical benefit

records.name: Radioligand therapy (beta emitters)
records.tldr: A target-binding molecule carries a radionuclide whose emissions deposit radiation in tissue. Distribution and retention help determine tumor and normal-organ exposure.
records.summary: Lutetium-177 therapies deliver beta-particle radiation through target-binding molecules. VISION tested PSMA-targeted treatment added to protocol-permitted standard care in selected, previously treated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. NETTER-1 tested lutetium-177-dotatate in progressive, somatostatin-receptor-positive midgut neuroendocrine tumors. Their clinical results belong to those populations and products, rather than every tumor expressing the target. Small molecules, peptides and antibodies have different distribution and clearance even when directed at a shared target.

links.label: FDA: nonclinical development of oncology therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals (2019)
MIRD pamphlet 22: alpha-particle radiobiology and dosimetry (2010)
EPA: activity, absorbed dose and their units
Sartor et al.: VISION, primary randomized trial report (2021)
Strosberg et al.: NETTER-1, primary randomized trial report (2017)

notes: Radioactive activity is a decay rate in becquerels; absorbed dose is deposited energy per mass in gray. A single bright image is not time-integrated exposure. Dosimetry combines suitable activity measurements or models over time with tissue geometry and emission properties. Neither the targeting-molecule mass nor the administered activity alone specifies tumor dose.

Radioimmunotherapy uses an antibody carrier. The broader radiopharmaceutical category also includes organ-seeking products without a separate targeting ligand. Not every attachment uses a metal chelator. Alpha and beta emissions have different path and energy-deposition properties; neither label alone ranks safety or effectiveness. Daughter redistribution and microscopic geometry can matter.
records.principle: Where the complete radioactive product travels, how long it remains and which emissions reach tissue jointly determine radiation delivery.
strengths: Targeted delivery of radiation through an accessible molecular feature
Emitted particles can reach neighboring cells
limitations: Kidney, marrow and other normal-tissue exposure can limit treatment
A positive scan alone does not establish absorbed dose or clinical benefit
Results from one radionuclide or carrier do not establish equivalence of another

records.name: Dosimetry
records.tldr: Dosimetry estimates the radiation energy deposited per unit mass in a specified tissue or target. The estimate depends on measurements, geometry and a stated model.
records.summary: Absorbed dose is reported in gray, equivalent to joules per kilogram. It differs from radioactive activity in becquerels, which describes decays per second. For a radiopharmaceutical, dose estimation uses the location and time course of radioactivity, the emissions and the target’s mass and geometry. Suitable calibrated serial imaging can inform the estimate; it does not turn one uptake value into a measured tumor dose. External-beam and internal-emitter methods answer related dose questions using different inputs.

links.label: EPA: activity, absorbed dose and their units
MIRD pamphlet 22: alpha-particle radiobiology and dosimetry (2010)
FDA: nonclinical development of oncology therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals (2019)

notes: Report the method, time sampling, target volume and uncertainty. An organ-average dose can hide uneven cellular exposure, especially for short-range alpha emissions. Absorbed dose and clinical outcome remain distinct; no single organ threshold or schedule applies to all products.

records.name: Radioligand dosimetry
records.tldr: Radioligand dosimetry estimates radiation deposited in tumors and normal tissues from where radioactivity goes and how it changes with time.
records.summary: Calibrated activity measurements, often from suitable serial SPECT or PET imaging, inform a time-activity model. Time-integrated decays, emission properties, tissue mass and spatial assumptions then inform absorbed dose. Equal uptake on an early scan can be followed by different retention and different doses. Administered activity is an input, not a substitute for patient- or tissue-level dosimetry. The estimates can support evaluation of dosing strategies, but improved outcomes from a particular adaptation require their own evidence.

links.label: MIRD pamphlet 22: alpha-particle radiobiology and dosimetry (2010)
EPA: activity, absorbed dose and their units
FDA: nonclinical development of oncology therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals (2019)

notes: Physical decay, biological clearance and radioactive daughters all affect interpretation. Alpha-emitter dosimetry may need additional microscopic considerations. FDA’s cited document addresses nonclinical development; it is not a universal clinical dosing protocol or evidence of a jurisdiction-wide reimbursement requirement.
records.principle: Estimate activity through time in specified source regions, then calculate the energy deposited in relevant target regions with explicit assumptions.
strengths: Makes tumor and normal-tissue exposure explicit
Can evaluate why the same administered activity produces different dose estimates
limitations: Calibration, time sampling and segmentation affect estimates
Organ averages can miss uneven microscopic exposure
Method-specific dose estimates do not establish a universal clinical threshold

records.name: Radio-antibody & radio-ADC
records.tldr: Radioimmunotherapy uses an antibody or antibody fragment to carry a radionuclide. Its radiation delivery and safety depend on the complete labeled product.
records.summary: An antibody provides recognition while the radionuclide provides radiation. This differs from releasing a small-molecule cytotoxic drug after intracellular processing. Attachment chemistry depends on the isotope and product; a chelator is not required for every radionuclide. In a historical phase 2 study, lutetium-177-J591 targeted PSMA in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer and produced substantial hematologic toxicity. That disease-specific experience does not establish current approval, breast-cancer efficacy or the suitability of every ADC antigen for radioimmunotherapy.

links.label: FDA: nonclinical development of oncology therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals (2019)
MIRD pamphlet 22: alpha-particle radiobiology and dosimetry (2010)
Tagawa et al.: lutetium-177-J591 phase 2 study in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (2013)

notes: Crossfire means radiation from one location reaching nearby cells. It is distinct from a diffusible chemical payload and does not require the same release chemistry. Neither crossfire nor an immune-effect hypothesis establishes clinical benefit after ADC resistance.
records.principle: The labeled antibody’s distribution and retention, radionuclide emissions and tissue geometry determine where radiation is deposited.
strengths: Can deliver radiation with an antibody recognition route
Particles can reach cells beyond the bound target cell
limitations: Circulating and normal-organ radioactivity can cause toxicity
Target expression alone does not establish sufficient tumor dose
Antibody and small-ligand kinetics are not interchangeable

records.name: ADC analytes and exposure
records.tldr: An antibody-drug conjugate and its released drug do not follow one shared concentration curve. The measured chemical form matters.
records.summary: A conjugate assay measures antibody carrying payload, or antibody-bound drug, according to the validated method. Total antibody includes conjugated and unconjugated antibody; unconjugated payload measures released drug separately. Active metabolites or catabolites can add further relevant species. Concentration, time course and exposure therefore belong to a named analyte. A conjugate dose in milligrams per kilogram is not the same quantity as the mass of free payload reaching a tumor or the blood.

links.label: FDA: clinical pharmacology considerations for cytotoxic ADCs (2024)
Ravenstijn et al.: translational and bioanalytical questions for dual-payload conjugates (2026 perspective)
Hamblett et al.: loading and exposure in one conjugate, cell and mouse experiments (2004)

notes: FDA’s 2024 guidance for cytotoxic small-molecule ADCs recommends validated measurements of the conjugate and relevant constituent parts, with later omissions justified by pharmacology, assay sensitivity and exposure data. It does not require every conceivable analyte in every study or automatically apply to every immune agonist or other cargo.

For a construct carrying different payloads, keep each chemical identity, loading distribution, release behavior and exposure distinct. A manufactured loading ratio does not establish the ratio reaching tissue over time. The same total DAR does not establish equal loading of each component or equal biological activity.

records.name: CHK1 inhibitor payloads
records.tldr: A CHK1-inhibitor conjugate carries a drug that interferes with a replication-stress checkpoint. A published conference abstract reports a HER2-directed preclinical example.
records.summary: CHK1 inhibition is the cargo mechanism only when the inhibitor is physically attached to the conjugate. The AACR 2026 abstract describes engineered-cysteine trastuzumab, a cleavable linker and a CHK1-inhibitor payload. The investigators tested cells and a HER2-positive breast-cancer xenograft model. This establishes a publicly described payload design and model experiment, separate from giving an oral checkpoint inhibitor alongside another ADC. It does not establish human safety, benefit after a TOP1 ADC or a treatment-selection rule.

links.label: Halazonetis et al.: CHK1-inhibitor conjugate, AACR 2026 abstract 1714

notes: The antibody delivery antigen and the payload’s checkpoint target answer different questions. The proposed advantage depends on sufficient intracellular release and checkpoint dependence, not a HER2 or replication-stress label alone. The conference abstract reports limited model safety observations; lack of mouse weight loss cannot establish human marrow safety or a clinical therapeutic window.

records.name: PARP inhibitor payloads
records.tldr: A PARP-inhibitor payload attaches a repair-targeting drug to an antibody. A published preclinical abstract describes a TROP2 conjugate carrying a PARP1-selective inhibitor.
records.summary: The AACR 2025 abstract describes a TROP2 antibody joined through a cleavable linker to a PARP1-selective inhibitor. Cell comparisons included the conjugate, free payload and antibody alone; a breast-cancer xenograft experiment compared their activity and blood-cell effects. The reported activity varied between tested cell models, illustrating that more delivery antigen is not sufficient to establish payload sensitivity. This is a conference-abstract proof of concept, not clinical evidence that antibody delivery reverses PARP resistance or removes systemic toxicity.

links.label: Koo et al.: PARP1-selective payload in a TROP2 conjugate, AACR 2025 abstract 5467

notes: An approved PARP-inhibitor pill, a free PARP drug combined with an ADC and a physically attached PARP payload are different products and evidence questions. Retain the actual conjugated chemical species, linker, release and exposure. A repair-gene variant alone does not prove the tumor’s current functional dependence or establish eligibility for an experimental conjugate.

records.name: ATR and CHK1 inhibitors
records.tldr: ATR and CHK1 inhibitors interfere with checkpoint responses to stressed DNA replication. Researchers test whether particular tumors depend on those responses enough to create a treatment window.
records.summary: ATR and downstream checkpoint signaling help cells respond when replication is stressed. Repair defects or other tumor features can increase dependence in specific models, but a gene name or stress marker alone does not establish patient benefit. A phase 1 camonsertib study enrolled selected advanced solid tumors with predicted sensitizing repair-gene alterations; a separate small prexasertib pilot studied previously treated BRCA-wild-type triple-negative breast cancer. These are different drugs, populations and designs. Blood-cell toxicity remained important, and neither study validates every proposed repair-defect biomarker.

links.label: Yap et al.: camonsertib phase 1 study in selected repair-deficient advanced solid tumors (2023)
Gatti-Mays et al.: prexasertib single-arm TNBC pilot (2020)
Duplessis et al.: single-payload ATR-inhibitor conjugates, AACR D3 2026 abstract A003
Halazonetis et al.: CHK1-inhibitor conjugate, AACR 2026 abstract 1714

notes: An attached checkpoint inhibitor is a distinct payload design. The AACR 2026 A003 abstract describes single-payload ATR-inhibitor conjugates, including TROP2-directed constructs, and reports isogenic repair-state comparisons and xenografts. The separate CHK1 abstract describes an engineered trastuzumab conjugate. These are preclinical conference reports, not human efficacy or marrow-safety results. A separately administered ATR or CHK1 inhibitor is a combination regimen rather than attached cargo.

Downstream DNA-damage or phosphorylation changes support a response in the stated model, not direct target engagement by themselves. Appropriate target, repair-state and exposure controls help distinguish delivery, inhibitor activity and cell susceptibility. Changing from a TOP1 payload does not guarantee bypass of a shared delivery or resistance defect.
records.principle: Inhibiting checkpoint signaling can impair a stressed cell’s response; exposure, repair state and other cellular processes determine whether that produces death.
strengths: Tests a repair- or replication-stress dependence hypothesis
Can be studied with DNA-damaging treatments using appropriate safety controls
limitations: Blood-cell toxicity can limit exposure
Biomarker and combination results belong to the tested drug, population and regimen

records.name: Histone lactylation
records.tldr: Lactate can contribute to a chemical modification of histone proteins. Experiments connect this mark to gene regulation in particular cell states and disease models.
records.summary: Lactylation adds a lactate-derived modification to histone lysine residues, rather than changing the DNA sequence. The original study identified this mark in human and mouse cells and investigated its timing and gene-regulatory effects in stimulated macrophages. A later mechanistic study in EGFR T790M-positive tumor models connected radiation, LDHA-dependent lactate production, histone lactylation and DNA-repair responses. Its cell, organoid and xenograft experiments provide a context-specific mechanism hypothesis, not a validated clinical radiation-selection test.

links.label: Zhang et al.: original histone-lactylation and gene-regulation study (2019)
EGFR-mutant metabolic, chromatin and radiation-response models (2026)

notes: Bulk lactate concentration, a particular histone modification, its genomic location, RNA output and DNA-repair activity are different measurements. The radiation study combined biochemical and chromatin measurements with genetic or pharmacological perturbations. A high lactate value alone does not establish that this mechanism is present, dominant or targetable in another tumor.

records.name: CAR-T cell therapy
records.tldr: CAR-T therapy uses T cells carrying an engineered receptor. Approved products treat selected blood cancers, with product-specific eligibility and safety requirements.
records.summary:
CAR-T cell therapy uses T cells carrying a chimeric antigen receptor to recognize a target. FDA-approved products include CD19- and BCMA-directed CAR-T cells for selected blood cancers, including B-cell leukemias, lymphomas and multiple myeloma. The individual product label defines the treatment setting and eligibility. A common autologous approach collects a person’s T cells, engineers and expands them outside the body, then infuses them back; conditioning and follow-up depend on the protocol.

A common antibody-derived CAR joins an external binding region, a hinge or spacer, a membrane anchor and intracellular signaling domains. The receptor is a protein; its encoding instructions and the living cell carrying it are different objects. Approved products and experimental constructs differ in cell source, receptor, manufacturing and clinical setting. Product labels and trial records define their actual uses; a platform name does not establish eligibility or benefit.

In early work, Gross, Waks and Eshhar joined antibody-variable regions to T-cell receptor components in 1989. Eshhar and colleagues subsequently tested single-chain antibody-binding regions joined to gamma or zeta signaling chains in 1993. These experimental designs helped separate recognition from the signaling machinery attached to it.

FDA-approved examples include tisagenlecleucel, axicabtagene ciloleucel, lisocabtagene maraleucel, brexucabtagene autoleucel, obecabtagene autoleucel, idecabtagene vicleucel and ciltacabtagene autoleucel. Their labeled diseases, treatment settings and eligibility differ; the individual product records retain those distinctions.

notes: Generation labels describe common signaling architectures. First-generation constructs use an activation domain, often CD3 zeta; second-generation designs add one costimulatory region; third-generation designs combine two. Fourth-generation and later labels vary across authors. More domains do not establish better patient outcomes. The full binder, spacer, anchor, signaling arrangement and cell preparation still matter.

CD28 and 4-1BB are borrowed intracellular signaling regions, not separately administered receptors. Kawalekar compared metabolic and memory features in defined human-cell experiments. Ramos co-infused two specified second- and third-generation products in lymphoma; different expansion and persistence did not isolate comparative clinical benefit. Neither study ranks all products by signaling-domain name.

Binding, surface CAR expression, activation, proliferation and completed target-cell killing are distinct readouts. Compare otherwise matched constructs, target-positive and target-negative cells, healthy-tissue targets and unstimulated activity. Hudecek found that particular IgG-derived spacers could support killing in a dish yet impair activity in mouse models through Fc interactions.

A peptide-HLA target is an exception to blanket HLA-independent descriptions. Rafiq tested a WT1 peptide presented by HLA-A*02:01 in cell and mouse models; this was a proof of concept, not evidence that every intracellular protein or every HLA type is addressable by that construct.

Relapse mechanisms need separate investigation. Sotillo found CD19 sequence and splicing changes affecting recognition in B-ALL relapse material and experiments. Deng found infusion-product transcriptional features associated with outcomes in a selected cohort of 24 large B-cell lymphoma infusion products; those associations did not prove that one engineered modification would correct every failure.

A 2024 preprint used a pooled signaling-domain library, repeated stimulation and single-cell sequencing to study how domain arrangement affected T-cell states over time. Its membrane-proximal-domain findings are construct-and-assay observations, not a clinical ranking of domains or a validation of pooled-screen hits as treatments.

FDA initiated boxed-warning changes in 2024 for the risk of T-cell malignancies after the then-approved BCMA- or CD19-directed autologous CAR T-cell products. Its communication calls for lifelong monitoring for secondary malignancies. This is a scoped regulatory warning, not a claim that every type of engineered immune cell has the same risk.

In June 2025, FDA eliminated REMS requirements for the named autologous CAR T-cell products in its notice. Product warnings and safety monitoring continued. The manufacturer postmarketing observational studies with 15-year follow-up described in that notice are different from the lifelong patient-monitoring statement in the earlier safety communication.

Lymphoma: failure comes in two shapes and they need different answers. Relapse without the antigen, through deletion, exon 2 mutation or selection for a spliced transcript the receptor cannot see (Sotillo 2015), is answered by changing the address. Relapse with the antigen still there is usually about the cells: single-cell sequencing of 24 axicabtagene ciloleucel products found three times the frequency of memory-signature CD8 T cells in patients who reached complete response at three months, and an exhaustion signature that tracked a poor molecular response at day 7 (Deng 2020). Collecting T cells earlier in the disease course, allogeneic and in vivo products, and armoured constructs are the responses to the second.
records.principle: A common CAR presents a binder outside the cell and signaling domains inside it, connected through a spacer and transmembrane region. Conventional surface-antigen recognition can bypass peptide-HLA presentation; specialized peptide-HLA-targeting CARs retain the relevant HLA and antigen-processing requirements.
strengths: Antigen-directed recognition in engineered T cells
Established uses for specific products in selected blood cancers
limitations: Shared healthy-tissue targets and inflammatory, neurologic or blood-count harms
Manufacturing, access and cost depend on the product and setting
Antigen heterogeneity, cell state, tissue access and local inhibition

records.name: Armoured, logic-gated & next-gen CARs
aka: T cells redirected for universal cytokine-mediated killing
records.tldr: Armored immune cells add a specified function, such as cytokine support or a changed response to an inhibitory signal. Each added function brings its own activity and safety questions.
records.summary: Armoring adds functions beyond a basic recognition receptor. Designs include continuous, activation-induced or surface-held cytokine support and modifications to particular inhibitory responses. A dominant-negative TGF-beta receptor is a receptor variant that interferes with signaling; it is different from deleting a receptor gene. Recognition logic and cell-elimination switches are separate design choices. None guarantees access to every tumor, coverage of antigen-negative cells or protection of healthy tissue.

links.label: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03373097: GD2-CART01 (Bambino Gesù phase 1/2)
FDA: CAR T-cell product design, testing and clinical pharmacology guidance (2024)
Liu et al.: one cord-blood CAR-NK construct in lymphoid tumors (2020)
Chmielewski et al.: inducible IL-12 and macrophage recruitment in tumor models (2011)
Chmielewski and Abken: TRUCK terminology and NFAT control (2012 review)
Narayan et al.: TGF-beta-insensitive PSMA CAR T-cell phase 1 study (2022)
Zhang et al.: inducible IL-12 TIL study and systemic toxicity (2015)
Chen et al.: endogenous-locus control of cytokine payloads in preclinical models (2025)

notes: TRUCKs is commonly expanded as T cells redirected for universal cytokine-mediated killing. Early CAR-triggered IL-12 experiments recruited macrophage-dependent activity against antigen-loss cells in tumor models; this did not change the CAR binder itself. Universal is part of the name, not a result of universal cancer killing.

The TRUCK framework describes NFAT-responsive inducible IL-12 expression. NFAT can also respond to physiological T-cell receptor stimulation, so activation-responsive is not automatically CAR-exclusive or tumor-exclusive. Induction, secretion, distribution and systemic effects must each be measured.

Liu studied one cord-blood CD19 CAR-NK product combining interleukin-15 support and an inducible caspase-9 switch. Its outcomes do not isolate the effect of interleukin-15. Narayan tested a PSMA CAR with a dominant-negative TGF-beta receptor in a prostate-cancer phase 1 study; a fatal event occurred with severe cytokine release syndrome and concurrent sepsis. Resistance to one signal was not resistance to every inhibitory pathway or every harm.

Inducible production does not establish confinement. In a separate melanoma study, NFAT-driven IL-12-producing TILs were associated with high serum cytokines and serious systemic toxicity. Those cells were TILs, not the same CAR construct as the earlier TRUCK model.

Use otherwise matched cells with and without the added function, with relevant suppressive signals, repeated stimulation and healthy-tissue targets. Cytokine concentration, viable-cell abundance and killing at a specified time answer different questions. Greater expansion alone does not establish a wider safety window.
records.principle: Specify the added gene or receptor, the cells carrying it, when and where it is expressed, and the response it is intended to change. Test its contribution alongside the behavior and harms of the complete product.
strengths: Experimental ways to address a specified inhibitory signal or add supportive activity
limitations: Local triggering does not establish local-only exposure
Added functions may also increase harmful activity
Component effects and whole-product clinical outcomes need separate evidence

records.name: Logic-gated therapeutics (AND, NOT gates)
records.tldr: Recognition circuits combine inputs to broaden target coverage or restrict activation. AND-like, OR-like, inhibitory and sequential designs have different failure modes and need direct testing.
records.summary: In cell-based examples, split and tuned activation/costimulation can implement an AND-like requirement, either-target recognition can broaden coverage with an OR-like rule, and a protective-antigen input can inhibit activity. SynNotch-to-CAR systems induce a second receptor over time, creating a primed state rather than requiring two antigens to remain simultaneously present on one cell. Thresholds, expression, decay and movement between tissues matter. An intended rule is a design hypothesis, not proof that healthy tissue is spared or that the complete product improves outcomes.

links.label: ClinicalTrials.gov: logic-gated CAR T
Kloss et al.: balanced activation and costimulation in tumor models (2013)
Zah et al.: CD19/CD20 OR-like recognition in tumor models (2016)
Zah et al.: experimental addendum on cell viability and OR-gate results (2016)
Fedorov et al.: inhibitory CARs in defined experimental systems (2013)
Roybal et al.: sequential synNotch-CAR circuit and priming/decay tests (2016)
FDA: CAR T-cell product design, testing and clinical pharmacology guidance (2024)

notes: Kloss combined suboptimal activation through one receptor with costimulation through another in specified tumor models. Two fully activating CARs do not, by themselves, establish an AND rule. Zah tested CD19/CD20 OR-like recognition; recognizing either target is a coverage strategy rather than proof of greater tumor selectivity.

Fedorov used PD-1- or CTLA-4-derived inhibitory receptors to restrain responses in defined experiments. Such a NOT-like recognition input differs from an externally activated switch that eliminates engineered cells. Receptor expression and the balance of activating and inhibitory inputs still need measurement.

Roybal used a synNotch input to induce a CAR for another antigen. CAR expression decayed after the priming stimulus was removed, rather than disappearing instantly. The studied bilateral mouse model did not show killing of the separate single-antigen bystander tumor. Whether another circuit remains active long enough to act elsewhere still needs a timing and tissue-distribution experiment; neither result establishes universal clinical safety.

Test A only, B only, both and neither, together with low antigen density, mixed populations, healthy tissues, repeated encounters and separated or sequential contacts. Activation, proliferation and completed killing are different outputs. Retain cell preparation, donor, cell ratio, timing and the units of each readout; a selected assay threshold is not a universal safe/unsafe boundary.

The Zah experimental addendum found that post-thaw viability over subsequent culture differed between donors and affected xenograft results, despite similar initial viability measurements. That result supports checking preparation and recovery; it does not validate a universal clinical viability cutoff or guarantee freedom from antigen escape.
records.principle: Define the actual receptors, signaling split, thresholds and timing. Measure the intended output for each relevant input combination and after the priming input disappears.
strengths: Can test combinations of recognition inputs rather than a single target
Coverage and selectivity can be explored as separate design goals
limitations: Stricter gates may miss tumors lacking a required input
Broader OR recognition may add healthy-tissue recognition routes
Residual activity, antigen density, manufacture and clinical harms need product-specific evidence

records.name: CAR-NK & CAR-macrophage
records.tldr: CAR-NK cells and CAR-macrophages add recognition receptors to different innate immune-cell families. Their native functions, starting materials and engineered support still matter.
records.summary: A CAR adds a recognition input rather than replacing the effector cell. NK cells retain activating and inhibitory receptor inputs; macrophages have different functions, including phagocytosis and antigen handling. Donor blood, cord blood, pluripotent-cell-derived products and NK cell lines are distinct starting materials. Product-specific manufacture, expansion, persistence, tissue access, compatibility and harms need their own evidence. A small favorable blood-cancer study does not rank every NK product as safer than every T-cell product or establish solid-tumor benefit.

links.label: Liu et al., CAR-transduced natural killer cells in CD19-positive lymphoid tumours (NEJM 2020)
Klichinsky et al., Human chimeric antigen receptor macrophages for cancer immunotherapy (Nature Biotechnology 2020)
Tang et al.: irradiated CD33-CAR NK-92 cells in an early AML study (2018)
Karre et al.: reduced self-MHC and rejection in mouse lymphoma models (1986)
FDA: CAR T-cell product design, testing and clinical pharmacology guidance (2024)

notes: In the 11-patient Liu study, cord-blood CD19 CAR-NK cells also encoded IL-15 and inducible caspase-9. No cytokine release syndrome, neurotoxicity or graft-versus-host disease was observed in that cohort, and low-level cells remained detectable for at least 12 months. This is neither proof of zero risk nor evidence for a uniformly short lifespan across CAR-NK platforms.

NK-92 is a continuously growing cell line, not a donor primary-cell preparation. Tang used CD33-CAR NK-92 cells irradiated with 10 Gy before infusion in an early AML study. Irradiation to limit proliferation makes its persistence question different from that of a cytokine-supported cord-blood product; the irradiation dose is not a universal CAR-NK treatment dose.

Reduced HLA display can reduce some inhibitory NK inputs, but activating signals, NK education and the actual cell-target pair still matter. CAR recognition, native NK activity and missing-self recognition are different inputs. An NK cell is not a natural killer T cell, and absence of a conventional TCR does not remove every compatibility, rejection or product-contamination concern.

Compare matched engineered and unmodified effector cells with target-positive and target-negative cells; retain donor/source, cell ratio and observation time. Attribution to a native receptor needs an independent perturbation with controls for changes in other ligands and target-cell viability. Binding, cytokine or granule release, viable-cell abundance and completed killing should not be substituted for one another.

Klichinsky engineered human macrophages and studied antigen-specific phagocytosis, inflammatory changes and tumor effects in cell and mouse models. These results describe a macrophage construct and those models; they do not establish a clinical efficacy or persistence ranking against CAR-NK or CAR-T.
records.principle: Add a specified CAR to an NK cell or macrophage and evaluate the receptor together with the cell family, source, engineering and native responses.
strengths: Different native effector functions can be investigated alongside CAR recognition
Some NK products have shown allogeneic feasibility in defined early studies
limitations: Persistence depends on source and engineered support
Host rejection, inflammatory harms and manufacturing quality remain product-specific questions
Cell and mouse results do not establish clinical benefit in solid tumors

records.name: NK cell therapy and CAR-NK
records.tldr: NK-cell therapies use natural killer cells, with or without an added CAR. Cell source and engineering determine what must be tested for persistence, compatibility, activity and harms.
records.summary: Natural killer cells integrate activating and inhibitory signals and can be prepared from different starting materials. Some products use donor or cord-blood cells; others use pluripotent-cell-derived cells or cell lines. A CAR supplies an additional recognition route, while cytokines or other engineering can alter subsequent behavior. Early clinical observations belong to the actual source, construct, conditioning and population studied. They do not establish universal compatibility, negligible inflammatory risk or uniformly poor persistence.

links.label: Wikipedia
Liu et al.: one cord-blood CAR-NK construct in lymphoid tumors (2020)
Tang et al.: irradiated CD33-CAR NK-92 cells in an early AML study (2018)
Karre et al.: reduced self-MHC and rejection in mouse lymphoma models (1986)
FDA: CAR T-cell product design, testing and clinical pharmacology guidance (2024)

notes: The cord-blood CAR-NK construct reported by Liu combined anti-CD19 recognition, IL-15 and inducible caspase-9. Its low-level detection for at least 12 months is a counterexample to assigning all CAR-NK cells a short lifespan. Detectability still does not by itself prove continuing useful function.

Irradiated NK-92 line products and nonirradiated primary-cell preparations answer different manufacturing and persistence questions. Tang reported 10 Gy irradiation for the studied CD33-CAR NK-92 preparation; that is a source-specific processing detail, not a universal protocol.

A comparison intended to isolate CAR-dependent killing needs matched effector cells without the CAR and otherwise matched targets with and without the antigen. Native NK inhibition and activation can change the result even when CAR binding is retained. HLA loss alone does not establish a favorable therapeutic response.
records.principle: Define the starting cells, expansion and engineering process, conditioning and administered viable cells; then measure native and CAR-associated activity in the intended context.
strengths: Potential for prepared allogeneic products in specified platforms
Native effector functions can complement engineered recognition under tested conditions
limitations: Host rejection, tissue access and inhibitory signals may limit activity
Persistence and repeat-dosing questions vary by product
Clinical benefit and safety require construct- and setting-specific studies

records.name: NK cell
records.tldr: Natural killer cells integrate activating and inhibitory inputs to respond to abnormal cells. An added CAR supplies another recognition route; missing self is one input rather than a guarantee of killing.
records.summary: Some inhibitory NK receptors recognize self HLA class I, while activating receptors respond to other features. Reduced self display can weaken an inhibitory input, but the NK cell, its prior education, activating signals and target context still determine the response. NK cells can also contribute antibody-dependent killing through Fc receptors. Donor-derived or engineered NK-cell products need their own compatibility, persistence and safety assessment rather than a blanket claim that matching or rejection never matters.

links.label: Wikipedia
Karre et al.: reduced self-MHC and rejection in mouse lymphoma models (1986)
Liu et al.: one cord-blood CAR-NK construct in lymphoid tumors (2020)

notes: The original missing-self experiment compared mouse lymphoma variants with reduced H-2 expression in defined hosts. It supports an immune-recognition principle, not a universal rule that every HLA-low human tumor is killed by every NK product.

A CAR, native NK receptors and cytokine support provide different inputs. The cord-blood product in Liu combined all of these design layers; a favorable observation for that construct does not isolate the CAR contribution or establish the same behavior for NK-92, donor blood or pluripotent-cell-derived preparations. NK and NKT cells are different cell families.

records.name: In vivo CAR-T
records.tldr: An in vivo delivery product carries receptor-encoding instructions into cells inside the body. Its dose is different from the later number and activity of engineered cells.
records.summary: Targeted delivery can supply CAR-encoding instructions to cells inside the body, using formats such as a viral vector or an mRNA lipid nanoparticle. This changes where engineering happens; it does not mean the active cells are donor-derived. Delivery targeting, cancer-antigen recognition, generated-cell abundance, receptor duration and useful function are separate questions. Conditioning, repeat dosing, safety and total cost belong to a specified product and protocol rather than to the in vivo label.

links.label: Pfeiffer et al., In vivo generation of human CD19-CAR T cells results in B-cell depletion and signs of cytokine release syndrome (EMBO Molecular Medicine 2018)
Rurik et al.: targeted mRNA nanoparticles in a mouse cardiac-injury model (2022)
ClinicalTrials.gov: INT2104 phase 1 oncology design, not an outcome report

notes: Pfeiffer generated human CD19 CAR T cells with a CD8-targeted lentiviral vector in humanized mouse experiments. B-cell depletion and signs consistent with cytokine release syndrome were observed. This was a preclinical study, not a human clinical response report or evidence for freedom from inflammatory toxicity.

Rurik used targeted mRNA lipid nanoparticles to generate transient CAR T cells in a mouse cardiac-injury model. It demonstrates a delivery/expression approach in that setting; it does not establish cancer efficacy, human safety or an interchangeable regimen for other delivery formats.

The INT2104 registry NCT06539338 identifies a phase 1 B-cell-cancer study in the dated source check. A trial design or registry listing does not supply efficacy results, prove local slot availability or validate a platform-wide claim about conditioning.

A prepared carrier can engineer the recipient's own cells. Vector or nanoparticle dose, ongoing delivery, newly generated cells, cell proliferation and receptor persistence should be measured separately. Stopping carrier administration need not immediately end the activity of cells already engineered.

The cited preclinical results do not by themselves establish a fixed cost reduction, universal absence of lymphodepletion or automatic repeat-dose feasibility. Evaluate the actual process, monitoring and protocol rather than treating these as inherent benefits of all in vivo products.
records.principle: Deliver encoding instructions into a defined cell population in the body, then measure which cells are engineered, where they go, how long expression lasts and what those cells do.
strengths: Investigates an alternative to administering cells engineered outside the body
May reduce some separate ex vivo manufacturing steps in a specified process
limitations: Cell targeting, off-target engineering and immune responses require measurement
Instruction dose does not specify final cell number or functional exposure
Conditioning, repeat dosing and cost are product- and protocol-specific

records.name: Cellular kinetics and persistence
records.tldr: A living cell therapy can change its number, location and state after administration. The starting dose, a sampled cell count and useful function are different measurements.
records.summary: After a cell infusion, measured abundance depends on division, survival and redistribution. In vivo engineering may also continue to generate newly engineered cells. A blood sample describes one compartment and time; it cannot count all cells in the body or establish entry into a tumor. Detectable receptor-encoding sequences, viable receptor-positive cells, persistent markers and functional activity should be reported separately.

links.label: FDA: CAR T-cell product design, testing and clinical pharmacology guidance (2024)
NCI: T-cell transfer therapy and harms
Liu et al.: one cord-blood CAR-NK construct in lymphoid tumors (2020)

notes: FDA CAR T-cell guidance treats exposure/kinetics, pharmacodynamic response, immunogenicity, identity, viability and potency as distinct assessments. Blood concentration-time measurements and optional disease-tissue sampling answer different distribution questions. A sequence assay is not automatically a count of viable cells expressing a functional surface receptor.

Keep the measurement method, time, compartment, units and denominator attached. A receptor-positive percentage can fall while absolute receptor-positive cells per microliter remain unchanged if the sampled denominator increases. Neither measure alone establishes an unchanged total-body cell population, tumor entry or antitumor benefit.

An administered cell dose is an input. The dose of a vector or particle used for in vivo engineering does not directly specify the later number of engineered cells. Autologous means the recipient’s own cells; allogeneic means cells from another person. Engineering outside versus inside the body is a separate axis; a prepared delivery product can engineer the recipient's own cells.

Expansion and persistence can prolong useful activity or harmful recognition. Stopping further administration does not instantly remove living cells or reverse an injury already triggered. A safety switch addresses a specified control mechanism; cell elimination, receptor shutoff and treatment of downstream inflammation are different interventions.

In the Liu cord-blood CAR-NK study, low-level detection at least 12 months after treatment belonged to a construct with IL-15 and an inducible caspase-9 switch. It does not establish the behavior of every NK-cell source or equate marker detection with continuing useful function.

records.name: Control of cell payloads by endogenous promoters
records.tldr: An engineered cell can place a payload under the control of a naturally regulated gene. The resulting expression pattern still needs measurement in the actual cells and tissues.
records.summary: A CRISPR knock-in can connect an engineered cytokine payload to regulatory control at an endogenous gene locus. In preclinical work, NR4A2 and RGS16 control supported cytokine expression in specified CAR T-cell settings, with tumor and safety measurements in mouse models. This is distinct from adding synthetic response elements to a separate promoter. Neither the locus name nor an activation-responsive design proves tumor-only secretion, clinical safety or patient benefit.

links.label: Chen et al.: endogenous-locus control of cytokine payloads in preclinical models (2025)
Guo et al.: synthetic NR4A-responsive payload promoter in human-cell experiments (2022)
Zhang et al.: inducible IL-12 TIL study and systemic toxicity (2015)

notes: Chen and colleagues screened endogenous genes and investigated NR4A2/RGS16 regulation for payloads including IL-12 and IL-2 in cell and mouse models. Patient-derived cells were also studied experimentally; that is not a clinical treatment result in those patients. The edited locus, retained native gene function, off-state expression, inducibility and persistence need characterization.

Guo and colleagues instead tested a synthetic NR4A-responsive promoter against a conventional NFAT-responsive promoter in human-cell experiments with weak stimulation. Reporter expression and improved proliferation in that system do not establish a clinical potency or safety ranking, and the synthetic promoter is distinct from an endogenous NR4A2-locus knock-in.

Keep trigger recognition, payload transcription, secretion, tissue distribution and downstream activity separate. The IL-12 TIL clinical experience shows why inducible production alone cannot establish confinement or freedom from systemic toxicity. Viable producer-cell abundance, time and cell state matter alongside cytokine concentration.
